title: Tax Documentation on a Host Payout Account and Withholding on a Claim Payment
content:
Where the tax documentation on a host's payout account is not in order, the marketplace withholds part of a payment released on a Keyturn Host Protection Plan claim. The marketplace's reporting mark is 600 of earnings booked in the twelve months before.

- Where the tax documentation on the host's payout account is missing or has expired and the earnings booked to that account in the twelve months before reach the marketplace's reporting mark, the marketplace withholds at its backup withholding rate of 24 percent.
- Where that documentation is missing or has expired and those earnings do not reach that mark, it withholds at its reduced withholding rate of 10 percent.
- Where that documentation is on file or is not required, nothing is withheld.

The withholding is taken from the payment as it stands once it has been rounded half up to two decimal places.

### Both sides of the mark

| Tax documentation on the account | Earnings booked in the twelve months before | Withheld at |
|---|---|---|
| shown as expired, or as requested and not yet returned | 600 or more | 24 percent |
| shown as expired, or as requested and not yet returned | below 600 | 10 percent |
| on file, or not required | either | nothing |

Earnings of exactly 600 reach the mark; earnings of 599 do not.

### The record consulted

The standing of the tax documentation and the earnings booked are read from the host's Keyturn Host Payout Account, the earnings being the trip earnings entered on its ledger within the twelve months before.
